paper.title_en: Interplay between long-range interactions and dissipation in quantum Ising model
paper.abstract_en: Long-range interacting models exhibit rich dynamical phenomena driven by deviations from collective descriptions. This work extends the study of these models to open quantum systems, focusing on the complex interplay between nonlocal interactions and local dissipation. The results demonstrate that the impact of long-range interactions on relaxation is twofold: they mitigate the impact of noises by stabilizing ferromagnetic domains and reducing local fluctuation, yet simultaneously accelerate memory loss by indirectly exposing each spin to a broader environment. While strong dissipation drives the system into glassy, range-insensitive relaxation, the results in weak dissipation regime reveal rich state-dependent dynamics. Specifically, long-range collective behaviors protect the early-stage coherence of systems quenched from polarized states, whereas they actively accelerate the relaxation of staggered configurations. Furthermore, nonlocal interactions continue to drive memory decorrelation even in the near-steady stages of a dissipative quench. These findings offer timely theoretical insights for the design, control, and calibration of analog quantum simulators operating with long-range interactions.
